scope: Four frozen-research correction candidates, current owner contracts, direct baseline credits and one optional-capability distinction. Offline static review only; no new research, native execution, or canonical edits.
counting_policy: Each owner-contract obligation counts once. Counterexamples are evidence, not additional findings. Existing F001 remains one original-baseline finding and is not a union extension.

repository_validator.structural_validation: Used validator_for and offline_schema_registry from the current repository gate.
repository_validator.semantic_validation: Called contract_semantic_failures for every case. Neither source_control_contracts nor jujutsu_integration_contracts has a semantic dispatch branch; both return []. Backup RestoreRun semantic checks belong to a different schema and do not validate these records.

candidates.proposition: The existing backup JJ restore-verification validation contract must reject ready_for_owner_activation when workspace_map_result is collision_blocked, colocation_activation_disposition is blocked_dual_writer_or_identity_collision, or working_copy_relation is unverified.
candidates.owner_basis: JJI-008 requires workspace/captured-file relationship truth before activation, explicitly blocks dual-writer or identity collision, and prohibits promoting blocked/conflicted results to successful activation. The readiness conditional enforces selected other prerequisites but omits these three result fields.
candidates.currentness: All three frozen counterexamples still pass current structural and repository semantic validation at the recorded HEAD and file hashes; positive and negative controls behave as expected.
candidates.distinct_from_F001: F001 concerns missing/non-null terminal command receipts. This candidate concerns contradictory readiness inside an already-present, typed BackupJujutsuRestoreVerificationReceipt. Adding a terminal receipt does not enforce this receipt content.
candidates.accepted_scope: One local readiness consistency obligation with three counterexamples. Keep Backup activation/readiness authority and JJ verification truth in their current owners. Add conditional or owner semantic checks and negative fixtures.
excluded_scope: No proven unsafe runtime activation.
No new event, command, handler, or Backup owner.
No automatic rollback/degraded-recovery feature adoption.
Do not infer every non-colocated owner-rebind disposition is invalid; the demonstrated cases concern explicit blockers or an unverified relation.

candidates.proposition: The existing SourceGraph contract needs enforceable relational validation of emitted node counts/page bounds, usable continuation on a current page claiming more data, unambiguous node identity, and a finite parent-reference expansion policy, rather than relying only on per-field bounds and boolean declarations.
candidates.owner_basis: SCS-017 already requires bounded pagination/hydration, stable node/edge references, identity preservation, and visible stale/partial state. Its current schema caps nodes and edges independently but accepts contradictory count/continuation/identity declarations and unbounded parent_refs. No repository semantic check closes these gaps.
candidates.currentness: All five frozen counterexamples still pass current structural and repository semantic validation at the recorded HEAD and file hashes; the 201-node and 601-edge controls are rejected.
candidates.distinct_from_F001: F001 governs terminal mutation/work receipts; this is a read-only graph projection consistency obligation. A required terminal receipt cannot repair page/count/node identity/reference validation.
candidates.distinct_from_other_candidate: The SourceGraph owner/projection and paging correctness predicates are independent of Backup JJ activation readiness.
candidates.accepted_scope: One bounded SourceGraph validation obligation with five witnesses. Require returned_count == len(nodes) <= page_size <= 200, current-page continuation consistency, stable node identity consistency, and a finite parent-reference policy. Exact adjacency bound/partial representation needs owner specification and cannot be inferred from the 600-edge cap alone. Cross-field rules may live in the existing semantic gate where JSON Schema cannot express them.
excluded_scope: No proof of a GG or Puppet Master runtime failure, performance result, or integration regression.
Do not require every parent ref to be present in the same page; cross-page ancestry is legitimate.
Do not impose a one-parent or arbitrary exact parent cap from the probe.
Do not count dynamic cursor ownership/generation or selection transition tests as separately discovered defects; those remain existing owner/runtime obligations.
Do not generalize current-page continuation rules to unavailable/partial/error pages without owner semantics.

candidates.proposition: The existing Jujutsu clone request/result contract must represent the legitimate destination-not-yet-initialized phase without requiring fabricated native commit/change/operation/snapshot identities; initialized repository operations retain their exact native fences.
candidates.owner_basis: JJI-002 defines revision/snapshot fields as exact native state and forbids synthetic workspace identity. JJI-003 and section 3.1 admit dedicated clone to a destination Source Location and cancellation settlement. Yet command_request.expected_revision, currentness.snapshot_id/expected_operation_id, and command_result.before_revision unconditionally require native values. No phase-discriminated absent-native-state branch exists. The pinned upstream clone code admits an absent/empty destination and calls init_workspace only after destination admission/creation; it rejects --at-op.
candidates.currentness: Current owner/schema retain the unconditional native identity preconditions. Current positive request/cancellation controls pass; absent native expected_revision, operation, snapshot, and before_revision are rejected at those exact fields. This is a representability gap established by schema plus owner/native phase semantics, not a conclusion that any existing runtime fails.
candidates.distinct_from_F001: F001 requires terminal attempt evidence to exist. This candidate asks how pre-init native state is truthfully represented even when the terminal receipt exists; adding receipt_ref does not permit absent native before-state.
candidates.distinct_from_other_candidates: Clone admission and pre-init identity are separate from graph projection consistency and restored-repository activation readiness.
candidates.accepted_scope: One existing clone contract correction. Distinguish reserved PM/destination identity and admission evidence from actual native identities, permitting explicit not-initialized state before init or a narrowly phase-restricted nullable representation. Bind subsequent checkpoints to observed native state, retain Host/Environment/catalog/currentness/lease/Permissions/FileSafe/idempotency/caller fences, and keep clone distinct from ordinary Git clone.
excluded_scope: No shipping clone failure or runtime certification claim.
Do not waive existing-repository native fencing or pass --at-op to native clone.
Do not manufacture an initial operation by adding a separate pre-init mutation solely to satisfy a request shape.
P26 C2 receipt nullability is existing F001 support, not a fourth correction.
A newly closed stage/settlement record or expanded cleanup/materialization diagnostics needs separate owner design; it is not counted here.

candidates.proposition: The existing neutral credential_lease must require use_http_path for HTTPS and known_hosts_receipt_ref plus forwarding_disabled for SSH, while retaining the existing true/nonempty constraints.
candidates.owner_basis: Source Control section 3.3 explicitly requires HTTPS path scoping and SSH known-host/no-forwarding binding. The schema conditionals constrain those fields only when present; neither the common required list nor the transport branches requires their presence. No current repository semantic dispatch applies to credential_lease.
candidates.currentness: All four frozen omission witnesses still pass the current schema and repository semantic validation. Complete HTTPS/SSH controls pass; existing false/null constraints still reject all five tested invalid-value controls.
candidates.distinct_from_F001: Terminal receipt presence does not constrain credential-lease transport evidence. These are different records and lifecycle boundaries.
candidates.distinct_from_F038: F038 says the broker/transport/custody policy is already chosen. This candidate demonstrates that the admitted machine contract fails to require specific already-mandated evidence. It repairs enforcement of that policy without proposing a competing credential architecture.
candidates.distinct_from_other_candidates: The transport credential-lease field-presence obligation is separate from graph relational consistency, restore readiness, and clone pre-init native-state representation.
candidates.accepted_scope: One transport-conditional required-field correction with four omission witnesses. Add required=[use_http_path] to the HTTPS then branch and required=[known_hosts_receipt_ref, forwarding_disabled] to SSH; retain const/nonempty constraints and current owner/field inventory. Add corresponding omission negatives.
excluded_scope: No demonstrated live credential leak, authentication bypass, or runtime security proof.
Do not treat a nonempty known-host ref as proof its referent exists or is current; consumer resolution remains a separate existing obligation.
No new broker, raw askpass path, secret-bearing field, command, persisted record, or ambient fallback.
Opposite-transport fields need not be made mandatory.

F001_credit.rationale: J0021 notes explicitly name receipt_ref nullability on failed/cancelled/recovery-required/effect-unknown terminal results, identify the owner requirement, record accepted malformed instances and negative controls, and propose requiring non-null terminal owner receipts. This is explicit discovery of F001, not generic cancellation commentary.
F001_credit.baseline_policy: Original 105-finding union and original evaluator-derived/no-arm-credit provenance remain unchanged. Add premium direct evidence in the continuation comparison only; do not create a second F001 or a current-canon defect merely from frozen rediscovery.
F001_credit.hybrid_credit_reason: Inspected hybrid terminal-receipt mentions describe covered existing requirements. They do not explicitly identify receiptless terminal schema acceptance. No hybrid F001 credit on that evidence.
F001_credit.currentness_boundary: F001 frozen discovery credit is separate from current repair status; no additional union extension or current defect is asserted here.

additional_baseline_credit_reviews.rationale: The original proposition explicitly includes failed native queries and traversal omissions becoming valid empty/list results. H15 identifies stream Err swallowed into Ok(LogPage), including initial traversal, and calls for partial/error/end distinction and initial/middle/peek injection. This is direct assertion of the same failure distinction, not merely a generic performance concern. It does not claim all file/type cases were independently studied.

H15 explicitly explains that both destination-edge endpoints may be descendants and must be rebased before insertion; it cites parent-relationship/no-divergence regression coverage and states lower-level primitives can miss command semantics. The original F088 rationale itself names GG insert-rebase divergence. This preserves the original merge-parent/descendant obligation and does not add an unconditional no-divergence rule.

optional_capability_review.proposition: Offer an evidence-gated user choice of object format when creating a new JJ repository, and show discovered effective format for existing repositories.
optional_capability_review.distinct_from_F050: F050 requires exact engine/CLI/repository-format qualification and truthful unsupported states. It does not require exposing a creation-time user selection control. Qualification is a prerequisite to the picker, not the picker itself.
excluded_scope: No approved default change, migration, universal SHA-256 support, or product adoption.
No additional finding for underlying certification matrix or format diagnostics already covered by F050.

root_resolution_after_independent_review.F110: The reviewer left symmetric historical credit to root. The original independent candidate status is preserved as authored.
